title: Marked-anodyne lifting, products and mapping objects
statement:
Use the universes and simplicial sets of [def-weil-size-convention] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A marked simplicial set is $(X,M)$ with $M\subseteq X_1$ containing all degenerate edges; morphisms preserve $M$, and product markings are coordinatewise. Write $K^ lat,K^\sharp$ for minimal and full markings, and $C^
atural$ for equivalences marked in a quasicategory. Write $\operatorname{Map}^\epsilon(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(X	imes(\Delta^n)^\epsilon,Y)$ for $\epsilon= lat,\sharp$. The marked-anodyne maps form the closure under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts of: (i) $(\Lambda_i^n)^ lat\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n)^ lat$ for $0<i<n$; (ii) $(\Lambda_n^n,E\cap(\Lambda_n^n)_1)\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n,E)$ for $n>0$, where $E$ consists of degenerate edges and the final edge; (iii) $(\Lambda_1^2)^\sharp\amalg_{(\Lambda_1^2)^ lat}(\Delta^2)^ lat\hookrightarrow(\Delta^2)^\sharp$; (iv) $K^ lat	o K^\sharp$ for Kan complexes $K$. A right lifting property means existence of a diagonal in every commutative square against the specified maps.

This class is generated by a small set: in (iv) countable Kan complexes suffice. Every marked simplicial set has a functorial marked-anodyne map to some $C^
atural$. A marked simplicial set has the right lifting property against this class to the terminal marked point if and only if it is $C^
atural$ for a quasicategory $C$. The pushout product $i\mathbin\square j$ of a marked-anodyne map $i$ with a degreewise injective marked map $j$ is marked anodyne; here the pushout product of $A	o B$ and $U	o V$ is $(B	imes U)\amalg_{A	imes U}(A	imes V)	o B	imes V$. For any $X,C$, $\operatorname{Map}^ lat(X,C^
atural)$ is a quasicategory and $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(X,C^
atural)$ is its core and is Kan. Restriction along any degreewise injective marked map is a Kan fibration on $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(-,C^
atural)$; it is a trivial Kan fibration when that map is marked anodyne. The same restriction is a trivial Kan fibration if the map is $A^ lat	o A$ described next: the underlying simplicial set $A$ is the quotient of $\Delta^3$ representing pairs $(\sigma,e)$ with $d_1\sigma=s_0e$, $d_2\sigma=s_1e$, and its marking adds to the degenerate edges the image of $\Delta^{\{0,1\}}$. In fact this last restriction is an isomorphism. All assertions are universe-relative and the marked-anodyne replacement stays in the input universe.
